title: The Riddle Tale
summary: Three women were turned into wild flowers growing in a meadow: two were red poppies and the third was a blue cornflower....
full_text:
Three women were turned into wild flowers growing in a meadow: two were red poppies and the third was a blue cornflower.

One of the women was permitted to return home to her husband every night under cover of darkness, provided she returned to the meadow before sunrise and transformed back into a flower among her sisters.

When morning dawned and the sun rose over the meadow, her husband walked out to find her and break the enchantment. He looked at the three flowers standing side by side in the morning dew, identified his true wife without hesitation, and brought her safely home!

How could the husband recognize her when the three flowers looked completely identical?

The answer is simple: because she had spent the night inside their warm cottage and had only returned to the meadow at dawn, there was no morning dew upon her petals, while the other two flowers were soaked in frost and dew! He plucked the dry blossom, and the loving wife returned to her human form forever.
moral: Quick wits and playful riddles turn ordinary chores into delightful amusement.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Riddle Tale"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
